answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a slow, stake-backed reputation grove rather than to raw identity count: each agent locks a small refundable deposit and earns standing only through completed tasks attested by independent peers over weeks, so spawning thousands of fresh identities gains nothing. A newcomer is like a lone juniper seedling - visible but weightless - while a sudden comet burst of identical new accounts triggers rate limits and stake slashing if their attestations cluster. Forging history then costs real time and capital, not just a script.
